entry.title: Why self-publishing pays off | No Ideas

media:group.media:title: Why self-publishing pays off | No Ideas
media:group.media:description:
Philip DiBello and Devin Washburn of Brooklyn-based design studio No Ideas take to the New York Nicer Tuesdays stage to talk about the creative process behind two of their largest book projects to date: Design Harder by Erik Carter and Figma’s 2026 Config zine. The pair discuss how taking a risk and building their own imprint, Book Ideas, led them on to even bigger projects and allowed them to find their own audience for their books through self publishing, or as Philip puts it: “If you build it, they will come.”
https://www.noideas.website/ https://nicertuesdays.itsnicethat.com/

entry.title: Interrogating crucial questions of our time through photography | Foam Magazine

media:group.media:title: Interrogating crucial questions of our time through photography | Foam Magazine
media:group.media:description: Chief editor Katy Hundertmark and former art director Hamid Sallali from Foam Magazine travelled all the way from Amsterdam and Spain to join us at our Nicer Tuesdays stage in September to talk about the origins of the acclaimed photography magazine, from the evolution of its constantly shifting and forward-thinking visual direction to thematic issues and how the team uses archival photography to create something more of a living creative medium than just another magazine. Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).

entry.title: Can motion design have a “body language”? | Studio Kiln

media:group.media:title: Can motion design have a “body language”? | Studio Kiln
media:group.media:description: Studio Kiln are behind motion design for MTV, Vinted, Netflix and even the Baftas, so that’s why Charlie Hockling and Nathan Smith joined our Nicer Tuesdays stage to take the audience behind the golden mask to learn how a brand can “have a body language” and craft, elegance and magic can be felt through expressive motion design. Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).

entry.title: The importance of doing “bad drawings” to develop your style | Joanna Blémont

media:group.media:title: The importance of doing “bad drawings” to develop your style | Joanna Blémont
media:group.media:description:
The V&A Illustration Awards-nominated illustrator Joanna Blémont understands the gentle balance between illustrating for big clients whilst simultaneously defining your own style – this is why she joined the Nicer Tuesdays stage in September to talk about the importance of doing “bad drawings”, moving into a tiny studio during lockdown to develop her practice and the 2,000 frame film she created in collaboration with a team of animators for Loewe. Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).

entry.title: Packaging is the only thing a designer can say to the customer | Mother Design

media:group.media:title: Packaging is the only thing a designer can say to the customer | Mother Design
media:group.media:description:
Mother Design is the independent brand and design company behind work for Ikea, KFC and even PG Tips’ classic monkey. Designers George Wu and Cecilia Serafini joined the Nicer Tuesdays stage in September to take our audience through just some of their packaging portfolio from soda drink cans to organic period care. In the process, the duo prove why branding communication needs to be loud and clear because packaging is the only thing a designer gets to say to a customer. Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).
https://www.itsnicethat.com/ https://www.motherdesign.com/

entry.title: Reimagining Crack Magazine with slime-inspired 3D motion design | Daisy Chain

media:group.media:title: Reimagining Crack Magazine with slime-inspired 3D motion design | Daisy Chain
media:group.media:description:
Harry Butt and Connor Campbell, the co-director duo behind motion studio Daisy Chain, shared the Nicer Tuesdays stage in July to walk the audience through their electric portfolio of colourful and dreamy animations. As well as that, the duo spoke about their collaboration with Crack Magazine, which included the task of making the average fly into a protagonist and putting their own spin on the mag’s identity using 3D graphics inspired by slime.
Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney)

entry.title: Transitioning from professional football to directing and photography | Alfie Whiteman

media:group.media:title: Transitioning from professional football to directing and photography | Alfie Whiteman
media:group.media:description:
Alfie Whiteman might be the ultimate multi-hyphenate: a former Tottenham Hotspur goalkeeper turned director and photographer. While playing professionally, he began building what he calls a "parallel life" in the creative world until the two could no longer run alongside each other. Eventually he traded a childhood dream for something less certain and more daring. At Nicer Tuesdays in July, Alfie told that story from back to front: the discipline carried over from elite sport, the long stretches of solitude that pushed him toward the camera and what it actually takes to walk away from one life and commit fully to another.
Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney).
https://www.itsnicethat.com/ https://www.instagram.com/alfie_whiteman/?hl=en

entry.title: Using mixed media as a narrative device for dual heritages | Jazz Grant

media:group.media:title: Using mixed media as a narrative device for dual heritages | Jazz Grant
media:group.media:description:
Multimedia artist Jazz Grant joined London’s Nicer Tuesdays stage in July hot off the heels of her group show Are We Really Here? The collagist draws upon her dual heritage and the vast potential of physical materials – and Jazz takes our audience through her career, from the origin of her interest in tactile animation to working with Gucci, Burberry, Hackney Central Library and The V&A.
Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney) https://www.itsnicethat.com/ https://www.instagram.com/jazzgrantstudio/?hl=en

entry.title: How painting offers self-discovery and connection with memories | Lily Kong

media:group.media:title: How painting offers self-discovery and connection with memories | Lily Kong
media:group.media:description:
Chinese illustrator and artist Lily Kong joined London’s Nicer Tuesdays stage in July once again to infect the audience with her typically optimistic outlook on art and design – in her own words, illustration is great at “bringing lightness to talking about seriously saddening problems”. Lily’s talk details how illustration practices can be used as forms of self-discovery through research, connecting with nature, practice and experimentation.
Special thanks to EartH (Evolutionary Arts Hackney)

entry.title: Tactile typography, paper cameras and graphic design as fine art | Kelli Anderson

media:group.media:title: Tactile typography, paper cameras and graphic design as fine art | Kelli Anderson
media:group.media:description:
Graphic designer and paper engineer Kelli Anderson joined us on the Nicer Tuesdays stage in New York City in a Q&A with Elizabeth Goodspeed to talk about her latest book Alphabet in Motion, an inventive, interactive pop-up book made entirely out of paper, along with her history with tactile typography. Kelli’s previous books include This Book is a Camera, a working 4x5 camera made from paper and This Book is a Planetarium, a publication that unfolds into a whole host of paper gadgets – and Kelli dives into her interest in Riso and hints at her upcoming project: a paper record player.

entry.title: Cataloguing Black mothers, Black astronauts and Black artists | Parallel Press

media:group.media:title: Cataloguing Black mothers, Black astronauts and Black artists | Parallel Press
media:group.media:description:
Founders of Parallel Press, Akoua Smith and renald Louissaint joined us on the Nicer Tuesdays stage in New York City to talk about how Parallel Press started up, its major projects and its newest publication Astro Black. This homage to Black astronauts is more than just an archive of boundary-pushing astrophysics, space travel technology and the people behind our most daring missions into the solar system, but a crucial protection of the archival materials from the Trump administration.

entry.title: Restoring New York City’s storefront signage through graphic design | Noble Signs

media:group.media:title: Restoring New York City’s storefront signage through graphic design | Noble Signs
media:group.media:description:
David Barnett, co-founder of Noble Signs, joined us on the Nicer Tuesdays stage in New York City to talk about what he loves most: signage, especially in the Big Apple. The graphic designer talked about collecting over 200 storefront signs in New York City and how the studio draws everything by hand, is shaped by reviving vanishing signage and how the team restores loved and lost signs to clients such as bakeries and delis.
